# I1
Verdict: strong-accept
CRITICAL: 0
MAJOR: 0
Headline: The closed synthetic evidence supports a substantial research opportunity in preserving safe continuations when pending outcomes interact with action dependencies (prior_work.md E1–E6).
Occupation: E1 already establishes synchronous frontier compression and its storage bound, while E2 establishes delayed belief updates; the attributable difference proposed in candidate.json is an output-sensitive frontier rule with continuation-preserving merging for their interaction. The complete full-method coverage in prior_work.md establishes no occupying target-setting result, and E5 analytically demonstrates why the interaction requires additional treatment.
Experiment: candidate.json specifies exact continuation comparison on six 6–12-action graphs, followed by 1,200 paired interruption seeds across 30 unseen graphs, three training seeds, and two delay levels. Validation-selected E3/E4 baselines, exact-log and no-memory references, matched budgets, and separate pending-tracking and merging ablations support attribution. Any equivalence violation kills the formal claim; a 95% paired interval excluding at least a five-percentage-point safety improvement at matched completion kills the empirical mechanism claim.
Estimand: Unsafe-continuation episodes divided by all interrupted episodes, evaluated with completion and memory bytes, directly addresses the proposed memory/error payoff; exact continuation comparison separately tests the preservation claim (candidate.json). Finite enumeration can falsify that claim, while the general guarantee remains a theorem obligation.
Payoff: E5 supplies a concrete causal reason to retain the joint pending-outcome/dependency information that simpler memories discard, and E6 makes compact retention consequential through its 128-token limit and prohibition on additional sensing or waiting. A successful frontier rule could provide bounded-memory continuation preservation unavailable jointly in E1–E4; neither the proposed rule’s correctness nor its empirical advantage is established by this evidence (prior_work.md; candidate.json).
Feasibility: The minimal experiment budgets two researchers, two A100 GPUs, 48 GPU-hours, 8,000 training trajectories, and CPU enumeration with frozen perception/control (candidate.json). This is a credible bounded first-paper proposal within review_contract.md’s resource criterion; the resource figures are estimates, not completed measurements.
History: unavailable.
Reason: Strong Accept is justified conditionally by complete coverage and low target overlap, the independently documented limitations in E1/E2, E5’s analytic interaction witness, E6’s external forcing constraints, and candidate.json’s controlled falsification experiment; these satisfy review_contract.md’s evidence-backed prospective-payoff gate without treating predicted gains as observations.
